## formal
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a generator of a horizon in the scope of Premise (N$_{+}$), a \emph{complex array} is an array of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3, weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, and a \emph{real array} the modes of one real chiral boson at integer weights $\kappa k$, which carries $-\kappa/24$ over a window $2\pi/\kappa$ in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering ($\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1) = -\kappa/24$, as each complex array does, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}(ii)). For a content with $f$ complex and $b$ real arrays per generator put $c = f + b$, and call the \emph{one-window test} the condition $24 \mid c$ and the \emph{two-window test} the condition $12 \mid c$. They are the conditions for $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = 1$ and $e^{2\pi Jc/12} = 1$ ($J$ the unit of the boundary-mode arrays; on the continuum light ray the unit is $I_{4}$ and the conditions are the same), that is, for a window evolution of the form $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$, with $P$ the grading normalised to $+1$ on the sea, to be $P$, respectively to be $\pm P$, equivalently the evolution over two windows to be $1$. That form is the reading under which the tests are posed; nothing below uses it. Call the \emph{additive reading} the reading in which the light-ray sea contains, besides the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation and in addition to them, one real array per real component of the null data of the gauge vectors, of the scalar doublets and, if $\epsilon = 1$, of the graviton. It lies outside the CAR scope of (N$_{+}$) and of the window reading, and it is not the reading of Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction} (J3), which identifies every channel of each four-dimensional massless field with the current boson of the s-wave theory, a current of the arrays. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Null data of each field, under the additive reading.)} On a null plane $N_{k}$ of $\Cl(1,3)$, $k = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$, $m = \gamma_{0} - \gamma_{3}$, $Q(k) = Q(m) = 0$, $\ip{k}{m} = 2$: every Weyl component gives one complex array for every mass matrix (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i)); every abelian gauge vector gives two real fields per generator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(ii)), at integer boost weight (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(vi)), and the same count for each component of a non-abelian vector is argued, not proved; and every real scalar component gives one real field per generator for every potential $V$: for linearised solutions $\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}$ of $\nabla^{2}\phi + V'(\phi) = 0$ the current $\omega = \phi_{1}\nabla\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\nabla\phi_{1}$ has $\nabla\cdot\omega = \phi_{1}\nabla^{2}\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\nabla^{2}\phi_{1} = 0$, its flux through $N_{k}$ is $k\cdot\omega = \phi_{1}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{1}$, which contains neither $V$ nor a transverse derivative, and $\nabla^{2} = (k\cdot\nabla)(m\cdot\nabla) - \partial_{1}^{2} - \partial_{2}^{2}$, so the field equation fixes $(m\cdot\nabla)\phi$ on $N_{k}$ from $\phi$ there and one boundary value per generator (that these data carry integer weight, so form a real array, is argued). Hence, under the additive reading, a content of $n_{g}$ generations of the slot module (sixteen Weyl components each, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(ii)), $n_{V}$ gauge vectors, $n_{s}$ real scalar components and, if a graviton's two helicities are counted, $\epsilon = 1$ ($\epsilon = 0$ otherwise) has
\[
c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon ,
\]
for every mass matrix and every scalar potential.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The gauge vectors drop out, additive reading.)} With the connection-forced algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$ (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}), $n_{V} = 12$ and the vectors contribute $24$, so they change neither test. A gauge algebra of dimension $d$ drops out of the one-window test if and only if $12 \mid d$, and of the two-window test if and only if $6 \mid d$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The verdict on generations, additive reading.)} With $n_{V} = 12$ and $n_{s} = 4n_{h}$ ($n_{h}$ doublets), the one-window test holds if and only if $\epsilon = 0$ and $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, and the two-window test if and only if $\epsilon = 0$ and $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$. So: with no scalar counted both hold exactly when $3 \mid n_{g}$; with one doublet the one-window test fails for every $n_{g}$ and the two-window test holds exactly when $n_{g} \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ ($c = 60$ at $n_{g} = 2$, where the window evolution is $-P$); with the eight real components of the linear rung field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}), $n_{h} = 2$, both hold exactly when $n_{g} \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, so $n_{g} = 1$ and $4$ pass and $n_{g} = 3$ fails ($c = 80$); with $\epsilon = 1$ (the graviton counted additively, as J3's species, every massless field, would include it) neither holds for any $n_{g}$, $n_{h}$ ($c \equiv 2 \pmod 4$). The content $n_{h} = 1$, $\epsilon = 1$ gives $c = 78$ at $n_{g} = 3$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The per-generation count.)} With $f$ Weyl components per generation and nothing else, the one-window test holds if and only if $24/\gcd(24, f)$ divides $n_{g}$ (the two-window test likewise with $12$), and the one-window modulus is $3$ exactly when $f \equiv 8$ or $16 \pmod{24}$. Fifteen components per generation (no neutral singlet, not a CPT halving of the slot module) give $8 \mid n_{g}$ and $4 \mid n_{g}$; sixteen components and the count of eight Majorana-Weyl units per generation give the same modulus $3$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Boson-fermion balance, additive reading.)} If $b = 2f$, the balance of on-shell degrees of freedom at which the quartic coefficient $2N_{V} + N_{S} - 2N_{W}$ of the attachment's Sakharov sum vanishes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}(iv), here with $\epsilon = 0$), then $c = 3f = 48n_{g}$ and both tests hold for every $n_{g}$; at $n_{g} = 3$, $N_{V} = 12$ this is that theorem's $N_{S} = 72$, with $c = 144$.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(J3's reading.)} If the integer-weight channels are read as J3 reads them, currents of the arrays, they add no array, $c = 16n_{g}$, and both tests hold exactly when $3 \mid n_{g}$.
\end{enumerate}
So the scalar and graviton content set the verdict only under the additive reading: there the tests single out $n_{g} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ only with no graviton and a number of doublets divisible by $6$ (one window) or $3$ (two windows), and with the graviton counted no content passes; under J3's reading the verdict is $3 \mid n_{g}$. Which reading holds, and so which fields form the sea, is not decided here, and neither test distinguishes three generations from six or nine.

## technical
The recorded recurrence test asks that the evolution of the light-ray sea over one window of Killing time be exactly the fermion grading, which needs the light-ray central charge $c$ to be a multiple of $24$; the weaker requirement, the grading up to sign or two windows giving the identity, needs a multiple of $12$. This result reads off both verdicts under two readings of the bosons. In the additive reading the null data of the vectors, the scalars and possibly the graviton are counted as real arrays of their own on top of the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation; this reading lies outside the CAR scope of (N$_{+}$) and of the window reading and is not that of the stored channel postulate J3, which reads every massless field's channels as currents of the arrays. Null data are mass-blind: a Weyl component gives one complex array for every mass matrix and an abelian vector two real fields (both stored), and a real scalar one real field for every potential, since the symplectic flux through the null plane is $\phi_{1}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{1}$ and the potential enters only the constraint; the non-abelian vector count and the integer weight of scalar data are argued. So $c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon$. The twelve gauge vectors give exactly $24$ and drop out; the recorded failure at $78$ comes from the doublet's $4$ and the graviton's $2$. With $n_{h}$ doublets, one window needs $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$ and two windows $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$; a graviton, which J3's species list includes, makes both fail always. On the two doublets of the store's linear rung field the test passes at one and four generations and fails at three; with one doublet the two-window test passes at two. At the boson-fermion balance where the stored quartic Sakharov coefficient vanishes, $c = 48n_{g}$ and the test does not see $n_{g}$. Under J3's own reading the bosons add nothing, $c = 16n_{g}$, and both tests give $3 \mid n_{g}$; the modulus $3$ comes from $24 = 8 \cdot 3$ against the power of two $16$, and the Majorana-Weyl count $8$ of the literature gives the same.

## lay
An earlier argument suggested that a timing condition on the sea of particles running along a black hole's horizon (after one cycle the sea should return to itself exactly, up to the sign that distinguishes fermions) would require the number of particle generations to be a multiple of three, provided only the matter particles form that sea. Whether the force carriers, the Higgs field and the graviton add to that sea depends on a reading the series has not settled: its own rule for these fields treats them as built from the matter sea, in which case they add nothing and the multiple-of-three answer stands. If instead they are counted as extra members of the sea, the force carriers add exactly a harmless amount, while the Higgs field and a graviton shift the answer: with one Higgs doublet the strict condition can never be met and a slightly weaker form picks two generations; with the series' two Higgs doublets it picks one or four and rules out three; with a graviton it can never be met. In no reading can the condition tell three generations from six.

## one-liner
For the one-window ($24 \mid c$) and two-window ($12 \mid c$) recurrence tests of the light-ray sea: if the null data of vectors, scalars and ($\epsilon = 1$) the graviton are counted additively, as real arrays beside the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation (a reading outside (N$_{+}$), the window reading and J3), then $c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon$, the twelve vectors drop out, the verdict is $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, resp. $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, and never with a graviton; under J3's reading, bosons as currents of the arrays, $c = 16n_{g}$ and the verdict is $3 \mid n_{g}$.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{The tests.} Let $J$ be the unit of the boundary-mode arrays, $J^{2} = -1$, central among the modes (on the continuum light ray the unit is $I_{4}$, and everything below holds with $I_{4}$ for $J$). For $c \in \Z$, $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = \cos	frac{2\pi c}{24} + J\sin	frac{2\pi c}{24} = 1$ exactly when $c/24 \in \Z$; likewise $e^{2\pi Jc/12} = (e^{2\pi Jc/24})^{2} = 1$ exactly when $12 \mid c$, and $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = \pm1$ exactly when $12 \mid c$. An operator implementing the grading is fixed only up to sign; normalising it by $P = +1$ on the sea, the one-window test says that $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$ is $P$, the two-window test that it is $\pm P$, equivalently that its square, the evolution over two windows, is $1$ ($P^{2} = 1$, $P$ commuting with the central unit). The form $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$ is the reading under which the tests are posed: each complex array carries $-\kappa/24$ over a window $2\pi/\kappa$ in the null ordering (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}(i), (ii)), and a real array at integer weights carries, in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering, $	frac12\sum_{n \ge 1}\kappa n = 	frac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1) = -\kappa/24$ (the zero mode carrying nothing), with excitation energies in $\kappa\Z$, so its one-window phase on excitations is $1$. \emph{Computed:} the finite part at $\varepsilon = 0$ of $\sum_{n \ge 0}(n + a)e^{-\varepsilon(n + a)}$ is $-	frac12B_{2}(a)$, by exact series inversion, so $\zeta(-1) = -	frac12B_{2}(1) = -	frac1{12}$ and a real array carries $-\kappa/24$; a real array at the half offset would carry $	frac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1, 	frac12) = +\kappa/48$, not the null-ordered window value. That the boson's zero point equals the null-ordered window value of the continuum, as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric} shows for the CAR arrays, is part of the additive reading, not derived. None of this is used in (i) to (vi), which are statements about $c$.

\emph{The two readings.} Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction} (J3), in the past cone of the null-ordering result, identifies each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel of every four-dimensional massless field with the current boson of the s-wave theory, which is a current of the arrays; read so, the integer-weight channels add no array and only the CAR count enters $c$. The additive reading instead counts their null data as further real arrays. Premise (N$_{+}$) and the window reading are stated for CAR arrays, so neither places vector, scalar or graviton data in the sea; the additive reading is an extension of both. Clauses (i) to (v) are statements under the additive reading and (vi) under J3's.

(i) \emph{Fermions and vectors} are the cited clauses: Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i) shows that every Lorentz-covariant mass term, Dirac or Majorana, acts from the right and enters only the equation fixing $\Lambda(k)\psi$ from the free data $\Lambda(m)\psi$, one complex channel per Weyl component; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(ii) shows that the flux of the Maxwell symplectic current through $N_{k}$ in the gauge $k\cdot A = 0$ contains the two transverse components alone, so an abelian gauge vector gives two real fields on each generator. \emph{Argued, not proved:} for the factors of a non-abelian algebra the count is that of the free field, component by component in the adjoint, the interaction entering, as the mass terms do for the spinor, only through the equations off the plane (light-front gauge); no stored clause covers it. Both carry integer or half-integer boost weight as recorded in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(ii), (vi): spinor data weight $	frac12$ (the complex arrays), vector and bivector data integer weight (the real arrays); clause (vi) of that theorem does not cover scalars.

"""synthesis.light-ray-recurrence-test-verdict-on-generations-is-set-by-the-scalar-content: exact checks.

The light-ray central charge c of a content is the number of complex fermion arrays plus real boson arrays on a
generator; the one-window test is 24 | c (the window evolution exp(2 pi I_4 c/24) P equal to the grading P), the
two-window test 12 | c (the evolution over two windows equal to 1, or U = +-P). J is the unit of the arrays.
(1) Scalar null data, in Cl(1,3) with k = g0 + g3, m = g0 - g3: for polynomial fields the divergence of
    omega = f1 grad f2 - f2 grad f1 is f1 box f2 - f2 box f1 identically, so a symmetric potential term cancels;
    the flux through N_k is k.omega = f1 (k.grad) f2 - f2 (k.grad) f1, with no transverse derivative and no
    potential; box = (k.grad)(m.grad) - d1^2 - d2^2.
(2) The count c = 16 n_g + 2 n_V + n_s + 2 eps, and the gauge vectors of the twelve-dimensional algebra drop out.
(3) The verdict on generations: one-window iff eps = 0 and n_h = 2 n_g (mod 6); two-window iff eps = 0 and
    n_g + n_h = 0 (mod 3); complete over one period of (n_g mod 3, n_h mod 6, eps).
(4) Fifteen components per generation; the general count f per generation.
(5) Boson-fermion balance b = 2 f gives c = 48 n_g; the Sakharov content N_S = 72 at three generations.
(6) A real array at integer weights carries (kappa/2) zeta(-1) = -kappa/24 (exact series inversion); under J3's
    reading (bosons as currents of the arrays) c = 16 n_g and both tests give 3 | n_g.
Clauses (1)-(5) are under the additive reading of the bosons.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import product

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

SQ = GA.sig(1, 3)                     # g0^2 = 1, g1^2 = g2^2 = g3^2 = -1
ETA = (1, -1, -1, -1)
PERIOD_G = range(3)                   # c mod 24 depends on n_g mod 3 (16 * 3 = 48)
PERIOD_H = range(6)                   # and on n_h mod 6 (4 * 6 = 24)
WIDE = range(40)
FERMION_TEST_RANGE = range(1, 97)
PER_GEN_RANGE = range(1, 49)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- polynomial fields in (t, x, y, z)
def padd(*ps):
    out = {}
    for p in ps:
        for e, c in p.items():
            out[e] = out.get(e, F(0)) + c
    return {e: c for e, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def pscale(a, p):
    return {e: a * c for e, c in p.items() if a * c != 0}


def pmul(p, q):
    out = {}
    for e1, c1 in p.items():
        for e2, c2 in q.items():
            e = tuple(x + y for x, y in zip(e1, e2))
            out[e] = out.get(e, F(0)) + c1 * c2
    return {e: c for e, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def pd(p, mu):
    out = {}
    for e, c in p.items():
        if e[mu] > 0:
            ne = tuple(x - (1 if i == mu else 0) for i, x in enumerate(e))
            out[ne] = out.get(ne, F(0)) + c * e[mu]
    return {e: c for e, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def box(p):
    return padd(*[pscale(F(ETA[mu]), pd(pd(p, mu), mu)) for mu in range(len(ETA))])


def mono(c, t, x, y, z):
    return {(t, x, y, z): F(c)}


PHI1 = padd(mono(3, 2, 1, 0, 0), mono(1, 0, 0, 1, 1), mono(-5, 0, 0, 0, 3), mono(1, 1, 0, 0, 0), mono(2, 1, 1, 1, 0))
PHI2 = padd(mono(1, 1, 1, 1, 0), mono(2, 0, 0, 0, 2), mono(-1, 3, 0, 0, 0), mono(7, 0, 1, 0, 0), mono(1, 0, 0, 2, 1))
WPOT = padd(mono(1, 0, 0, 0, 0), mono(2, 1, 1, 0, 0), mono(-1, 0, 0, 0, 2))     # V'' along a background


def vec(*cs):
    return GA.add(*[GA.scal(c, GA.gen(i)) for i, c in enumerate(cs)])


def components(v):
    """contravariant components v^mu of a vector v = v^mu g_mu"""
    return [v.get((mu,), F(0)) for mu in range(len(ETA))]


def directional(v, p):
    return padd(*[pscale(c, pd(p, mu)) for mu, c in enumerate(components(v))])


def current(f1, f2):
    """omega^mu = eta^{mu mu}(f1 d_mu f2 - f2 d_mu f1): omega = f1 grad f2 - f2 grad f1"""
    return [pscale(F(ETA[mu]), padd(pmul(f1, pd(f2, mu)), pscale(F(-1), pmul(f2, pd(f1, mu)))))
            for mu in range(len(ETA))]


def check_scalar_null_data_carries_no_potential():
    premise("synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components")
    premise("synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays")
    premise("synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators")
    k, m = vec(1, 0, 0, 1), vec(1, 0, 0, -1)
    GA.check("k is null", GA.mul(k, k, SQ) == {})
    GA.check("m is null", GA.mul(m, m, SQ) == {})
    GA.check("<k, m> = 2", GA.dot(k, m, SQ) == 2)
    om = current(PHI1, PHI2)
    div = padd(*[pd(om[mu], mu) for mu in range(len(ETA))])
    rhs = padd(pmul(PHI1, box(PHI2)), pscale(F(-1), pmul(PHI2, box(PHI1))))
    GA.check("div omega = f1 box f2 - f2 box f1 identically", div == rhs)
    # on linearised solutions box f = -W f (W = V'' symmetric): the divergence is f1(-W f2) - f2(-W f1) = 0
    lin = padd(pmul(PHI1, pscale(F(-1), pmul(WPOT, PHI2))), pscale(F(-1), pmul(PHI2, pscale(F(-1), pmul(WPOT, PHI1)))))
    GA.check("the potential term cancels from the divergence", lin == {})
    # flux through N_k: k . omega with omega = omega^mu g_mu, k . g_mu from the algebra
    kdot = [GA.dot(k, GA.gen(mu), SQ) for mu in range(len(ETA))]
    flux = padd(*[pscale(kdot[mu], om[mu]) for mu in range(len(ETA))])
    want = padd(pmul(PHI1, directional(k, PHI2)), pscale(F(-1), pmul(PHI2, directional(k, PHI1))))
    GA.check("flux k.omega = f1 (k.grad) f2 - f2 (k.grad) f1", flux == want)
    # no transverse derivative and no potential enter: k.grad = d_t + d_z
    GA.check("k.grad = d_t + d_z", directional(k, PHI2) == padd(pd(PHI2, 0), pd(PHI2, 3)))
    GA.check("m.grad = d_t - d_z", directional(m, PHI2) == padd(pd(PHI2, 0), pscale(F(-1), pd(PHI2, 3))))
    for p in (PHI1, PHI2, pmul(PHI1, PHI2)):
        fact = padd(directional(k, directional(m, p)), pscale(F(-1), pd(pd(p, 1), 1)), pscale(F(-1), pd(pd(p, 2), 2)))
        GA.check("box = (k.grad)(m.grad) - d_1^2 - d_2^2", fact == box(p))
    # control: through a constant-time surface (normal g0) the flux f1 d_t f2 - f2 d_t f1 differs
    e0 = vec(1, 0, 0, 0)
    t_flux = padd(pmul(PHI1, directional(e0, PHI2)), pscale(F(-1), pmul(PHI2, directional(e0, PHI1))))
    GA.check("control: the timelike flux differs from the null flux", t_flux != flux)
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the light-ray central charge of a content
def charge(n_g, n_V, n_s, eps, per_gen=16):
    return per_gen * n_g + 2 * n_V + n_s + 2 * eps


def one_window(c):
    return F(c, 24).denominator == 1


def two_window(c):
    return F(c, 12).denominator == 1


def check_content_count_and_gauge_vectors_drop_out():
    premise("synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components")
    premise("synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators")
    premise("standard-model.connection-forced")
    premise("synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum")
    GA.check("the recorded content: c = 78 at three generations, one doublet, a graviton", charge(3, 12, 4, 1) == 78)
    GA.check("spin-1/2 content alone at three generations: 48", charge(3, 0, 0, 0) == 48)
    GA.check("with the vectors: 72", charge(3, 12, 0, 0) == 72)
    GA.check("with the linear rung field's eight components: 80", charge(3, 12, 8, 0) == 80)
    GA.check("the twelve vectors carry 24", charge(0, 12, 0, 0) == 24)
    GA.check("the twelve vectors pass both tests", one_window(24) and two_window(24))
    for d in WIDE:
        GA.check("a d-dimensional gauge algebra drops out of the one-window test iff 12 | d",
                 one_window(charge(0, d, 0, 0)) == (d % 12 == 0))
        GA.check("and out of the two-window test iff 6 | d", two_window(charge(0, d, 0, 0)) == (d % 6 == 0))
    GA.check("contrast: 45 vectors (so(10)) give 90, which fails", not two_window(charge(0, 45, 0, 0)))
    # the window phase where it is a quarter turn: a unit J with J^2 = -1 (here g1 g2 of Cl(1,3), standing for the
    # boundary-mode unit), exp(2 pi J c/24) = J^(c/6)
    J = GA.mul(GA.gen(1), GA.gen(2), SQ)
    GA.check("J^2 = -1", GA.mul(J, J, SQ) == GA.sc(-1))
    GA.check("the vectors' one-window phase J^4 = 1", GA.mul(GA.mul(J, J, SQ), GA.mul(J, J, SQ), SQ) == GA.sc(1))
    return True


def check_verdict_on_generations():
    premise("synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric")
    premise("standard-model.connection-forced")
    premise("synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum")
    # complete over one period: c mod 24 depends on (n_g mod 3, n_h mod 6, eps)
    for n_g, n_h, eps in product(PERIOD_G, PERIOD_H, (0, 1)):
        for lift_g, lift_h in ((0, 0), (3, 6), (6, 12)):
            c = charge(n_g + lift_g, 12, 4 * (n_h + lift_h), eps)
            GA.check("one-window iff eps = 0 and n_h = 2 n_g mod 6",
                     one_window(c) == (eps == 0 and (n_h - 2 * n_g) % 6 == 0))
            GA.check("two-window iff eps = 0 and n_g + n_h = 0 mod 3",
                     two_window(c) == (eps == 0 and (n_g + n_h) % 3 == 0))
    for n_g, n_h in product(WIDE, WIDE):
        c = charge(n_g, 12, 4 * n_h, 0)
        GA.check("one-window rule on a wide range", one_window(c) == ((n_h - 2 * n_g) % 6 == 0))
        GA.check("a graviton fails both tests: c = 2 mod 4", (c + 2) % 4 == 2 and not two_window(c + 2))
    passes = lambda test, n_h: [g for g in range(1, 10) if test(charge(g, 12, 4 * n_h, 0))]
    GA.check("no scalars: both tests pass at n_g = 3, 6, 9", passes(one_window, 0) == [3, 6, 9] == passes(two_window, 0))
    GA.check("one doublet: the one-window test never passes", passes(one_window, 1) == [])
    GA.check("one doublet: the two-window test passes at n_g = 2, 5, 8", passes(two_window, 1) == [2, 5, 8])
    GA.check("two doublets: both pass at n_g = 1, 4, 7", passes(one_window, 2) == [1, 4, 7] == passes(two_window, 2))
    GA.check("two generations with one doublet: c = 60", charge(2, 12, 4, 0) == 60)
    J = GA.mul(GA.gen(1), GA.gen(2), SQ)
    Jp = lambda n: GA.sc(1) if n == 0 else GA.mul(J, Jp(n - 1), SQ)
    GA.check("c = 60: the one-window phase J^10 = -1 (U = -P)", Jp(60 // 6) == GA.sc(-1))
    GA.check("c = 60: the two-window phase J^20 = 1", Jp(2 * 60 // 6) == GA.sc(1))
    GA.check("c = 60: U = -P passes the sign-free form 12 | c", two_window(60) and not one_window(60))
    return True


def check_neutral_singlet_and_the_per_generation_count():
    premise("synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components")
    for n_g in FERMION_TEST_RANGE:
        c15 = charge(n_g, 0, 0, 0, per_gen=15)
        GA.check("fifteen per generation: one-window iff 8 | n_g", one_window(c15) == (n_g % 8 == 0))
        GA.check("fifteen per generation: two-window iff 4 | n_g", two_window(c15) == (n_g % 4 == 0))
    for f in PER_GEN_RANGE:
        q = (F(24) / _gcd(24, f)).numerator
        for n_g in FERMION_TEST_RANGE:
            GA.check("f per generation: one-window iff 24/gcd(24, f) | n_g",
                     one_window(charge(n_g, 0, 0, 0, per_gen=f)) == (n_g % q == 0))
        q2 = (F(12) / _gcd(12, f)).numerator
        for n_g in FERMION_TEST_RANGE:
            GA.check("f per generation: two-window iff 12/gcd(12, f) | n_g",
                     two_window(charge(n_g, 0, 0, 0, per_gen=f)) == (n_g % q2 == 0))
        GA.check("the modulus is 3 exactly when f = 8 or 16 mod 24", (q == 3) == (f % 24 in (8, 16)))
    GA.check("sixteen and eight (Majorana-Weyl count) give the same modulus 3",
             (F(24) / _gcd(24, 16)) == (F(24) / _gcd(24, 8)) == 3)
    return True


def _gcd(a, b):
    while b:
        a, b = b, a % b
    return a


def check_boson_fermion_balance_passes_every_generation_number():
    premise("synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations")
    for n_g in WIDE:
        f = 16 * n_g
        b = 2 * f
        GA.check("balance b = 2f gives c = 48 n_g", f + b == 48 * n_g)
        GA.check("and both tests pass", one_window(f + b) and two_window(f + b))
    # the stored quartic coefficient 2 N_V + N_S - 2 N_W vanishes at N_g = 3, N_V = 12 only for N_S = 72
    N_W = 16 * 3
    N_S = 2 * N_W - 2 * 12
    GA.check("N_S = 72", N_S == 72)
    GA.check("the Sakharov-balanced content has c = 144", charge(3, 12, N_S, 0) == 144)
    GA.check("144 = 6 * 24", one_window(charge(3, 12, N_S, 0)) and F(144, 24) == 6)
    GA.check("control: removing one scalar breaks it", not one_window(charge(3, 12, N_S - 1, 0)))
    return True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the zero point of a real array, and J3's reading
SERIES_ORDER = 6


def _exp_series(a, n):
    """coefficients of e^{-a eps} up to eps^(n-1)"""
    out, term = [], F(1)
    for j in range(n):
        out.append(term)
        term = term * (-a) / F(j + 1)
    return out


def _series_mul(x, y, n):
    return [sum((x[i] * y[j - i] for i in range(j + 1)), F(0)) for j in range(n)]


def _series_inv(x, n):
    inv = [F(1) / x[0]]
    for j in range(1, n):
        inv.append(-sum((x[i] * inv[j - i] for i in range(1, j + 1)), F(0)) / x[0])
    return inv


def finite_part(a):
    """finite part at eps = 0 of sum_{n >= 0} (n + a) e^{-eps (n + a)} = -h'(eps), h = e^{-a eps}/(1 - e^{-eps});
    eps h = sum c_j eps^j, and the eps^0 coefficient of -h' is -c_2"""
    n = SERIES_ORDER
    em1 = _exp_series(F(1), n + 1)
    q = [-em1[j + 1] for j in range(n)]                  # (1 - e^{-eps})/eps
    eh = _series_mul(_exp_series(a, n), _series_inv(q, n), n)
    return -eh[2]


def bernoulli2(a):
    return a * a - a + F(1, 6)


def check_real_array_zero_point_and_the_j3_reading():
    premise("synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric")
    premise("synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components")
    for a in (F(1), F(1, 2), F(1, 3), F(2, 5)):
        GA.check("finite part is -B_2(a)/2", finite_part(a) == -bernoulli2(a) / 2)
    GA.check("zeta(-1) = -1/12", finite_part(F(1)) == F(-1, 12))
    # a real chiral boson at integer weights: (kappa/2) sum_{n >= 1} n = (kappa/2) zeta(-1) = -kappa/24
    for kappa in (F(1, 4), F(3), F(2, 7)):
        GA.check("a real array carries -kappa/24", kappa / 2 * finite_part(F(1)) == -kappa / 24)
        GA.check("at the half offset it would carry +kappa/48", kappa / 2 * finite_part(F(1, 2)) == kappa / 48)
        GA.check("a complex array at the half offset carries -kappa/24 (CAR sign)",
                 -kappa / 2 * 2 * finite_part(F(1, 2)) == -kappa / 24)
    # J3's reading: the integer-weight channels are currents of the arrays and add nothing, c = 16 n_g
    j3 = [g for g in range(1, 10) if one_window(charge(g, 0, 0, 0))]
    GA.check("J3 reading: one-window passes exactly n_g = 3, 6, 9", j3 == [3, 6, 9])
    GA.check("J3 reading: two-window passes exactly n_g = 3, 6, 9",
             [g for g in range(1, 10) if two_window(charge(g, 0, 0, 0))] == [3, 6, 9])
    GA.check("contrast: the additive reading with one doublet and a graviton fails at three", not two_window(78))
    return True
